script.base: Book script is Tampa control: implied totals TB 25.0 / CLE 16.5 on a 41.5 outdoor total, so TB leads by halftime or late, pace stays moderate, and the leader leans run (Bucky Irving carry bump) while Cleveland (16.5) is chasing. Tampa blitzed 46% in its only game and Cleveland's offense was -1.01 EPA/dropback vs blitz vs +0.23 unblitzed, so CLE explosives stall and drives shorten rather than become a shootout.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and both unders lost because week-1 blitz rate was opponent-specific and Tampa sat in zone, so Watson's +0.23 unblitzed EPA showed up and Boston turned another 40-yard shot — the same 114-air-yard profile — into a second 59-plus, helped if Killebrew was inactive and the middle (13.5 YPA on 4 throws) stayed a bust. Judkins lost the under because Cleveland never trailed by two scores: Watson's legs kept them on schedule, the backup guard held, Judkins got a carry spike plus one of the 10+ runs Tampa already allows, and 33.5 was only half a yard above a 12-carry game. A late CLE garbage drive can also cash Boston after the script read was otherwise right. The counter-case is real on sample size; that is why both are leans, flagged, and unpriced, not strong bets.
slip_story: One story only: Tampa leads, blitzes, Cleveland stalls. Stack is Judkins rushyds under (negative script + Jenkins out) with Boston recyds under (pressure kills the 114-air-yard shot). They win together in the base script and the blowout flip; they both die if CLE hangs around and TB stops blitzing, so do not add CLE overs, a game over, or Egbuka/Boston overs. Irving rush over would fit the late-clock half of this story but his 45.5 line is an efficiency repeat on 8 carries, so it stays off the slip. Not a 3-4 leg ticket by itself; no TD legs; one market per player.
